---
title: "Reports from supplied posterior summaries"
subtitle: "T.1 · browser-local inputs and declared report families"
description: "Local calculation from normal summaries, declared priors or pairwise probability matrices."
---

The tool builds a grade report from posterior means and standard deviations, estimates with standard errors
and a prior, or pairwise probability matrices. The result names the set of reports searched. The calculation
runs in your browser, where your input records stay.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/your-data.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["your-data"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Eight posterior summaries** uses the first 8 units from the league example, which differ in precision.
  The report states 17 pairs and has weighted risk .1455.
- **Eight estimates, flat prior** uses a normal posterior for each unit, centered on its estimate with SD
  equal to its SE. The grades agree with the first example even though the posterior probabilities and risk differ. Here the risk is .1368.
- **Eight estimates, Normal prior** centers the prior at zero with SD .15. The posterior matches the first example, and the risk is .1455. The prior is a separate assumption from the estimates and their SEs.
- **Two probability matrices** uses the supplied probabilities for two criteria at six sites. The common
  report states 9 pairs at weighted risk .0933. The matrices provide pair probabilities without site means or intervals.
- **Thirty posterior summaries** exceeds the enumeration limit. The tool searches cuts of the weighted
  expected-rank order, which depends on the criterion weights. The best report in that order states 251 pairs at risk .1581.
- **All reports tied** has 541 reports with the same minimum risk. The list displays the first 100 and gives
  the total. With every comparison withheld, the expected error share is shown as NA.

The normal-input calculation assumes that the units are independent given the model. Use joint draws or a joint
law in R when the units are correlated. For matrices, specify the event and where the probabilities came from.
The input assumes zero probability of latent equality and a zero comparison margin. The checks cover dimensions,
ranges, and whether opposite directions sum to one. A joint law, calibration, and numerical accuracy need
separate evidence. Leave unassessed units out of the input because a bottom grade would assert comparisons about them.

Apply keeps the previous report until the new input passes the checks. A download includes the input and settings
used in the displayed report. The URL carries settings only, so paste the records and source descriptions again
after a reload. If you open the optional joint solver, its status and gap describe the search using the supplied probabilities.

[Open the standalone tool](../../embed/your-data.html?preset=league8-posterior).

Related applications: [Grade reports as pairwise decisions](../grades/report-builder.qmd) · [The matrix of pairwise posterior probabilities](../uncertainty/pairwise-matrix.qmd) · [Computation of optimal grade reports](../grades/computing-grades.qmd).
